title: Riglane MCP Server Contract
description: Schemas for the workflow-engine MCP server's tool surface. Each tool has paired input + output definitions. Two additional definitions cover the success/error envelope used for all tools/call responses.

tool_call_success.description: Wrapper used by the engine for every successful tool/call response. The 'content' array always contains a single text item; the text is a JSON-serialized tool result.

tool_call_error.description: Wrapper used by the engine for tool/call responses that failed inside the handler (caught exceptions or unknown tool names). isError MUST be true. JSON-RPC error envelope is NOT used for tool failures.

engine_action.description: The complete engine action vocabulary — every `action` value a workflow_engine tool can return. Per-tool outputs constrain to their own subset: step_begin refuses with BLOCKED_OUT_OF_ORDER / BLOCKED_PARTIAL_FAILURE / BLOCKED_LANES_ACTIVE / BLOCKED_FOREIGN_CALLER; step_collect_result decides with PROCEED / RETRY_STEP / STOP_WORKFLOW and refuses with BLOCKED_FOREIGN_CALLER (VERIFY_MANUALLY is historical — a verdict for a different step is now re-validated inline instead of asking for arbitration; kept so old artifacts validate); step_complete carries the control-flow actions (LOOP_BACK / ENTER_ROUTE / ENTER_LANES / LANE_WAIT / AWAITING_LOOP_DECISION / AWAITING_ROUTE_DECISION) on success envelopes — successful advances with a known target also carry the next step's begin payload (next_begin; lanes_begin per lane on ENTER_LANES) and FIX_AND_RETRY / STOP_WORKFLOW / USER_REJECTED / AWAITING_HUMAN_RESPONSE / BLOCKED_PARTIAL_FAILURE / BLOCKED_LANES_FAILED (the join barrier refused) / BLOCKED_FOREIGN_CALLER on error envelopes. BLOCKED_PLANNING_FAILURE belongs to the dynamic-planning tools, which this schema does not (yet) cover — it is listed so the vocabulary is complete in one place.

params.description: User-provided params (key-value pairs). Engine merges with workflow.yaml param defaults; user values win.

oneOf.description: Success: a new run is initialized.

external_channel.description: Present when the workflow declares a human gate (or loop/route decider) answered outside the terminal. The engine brings the local server up early so a consumer can read `discovery` for the live base URL + token; it is a declaration, not a verification — the guarantee that a question is answerable is enforced when the message is posted.

next_begin.description: Composite driving: the FIRST step's complete step_begin payload, composed at init (dynamic child inits included — workflow_invoke_dynamic forwards it) — drive from it directly, do not call step_begin for it. Absent = the old protocol (degraded compose, blocked tools).

oneOf.description: workflow_init rejection. Top-level runs mint a unique per-run dir and run in parallel; this fires only when a reused runtime_dir (dynamic child / externally-managed run) already holds an in-progress run.

run_id.description: Which run to resume. Omitted: the latest resumable run of this workflow. Named: that run, or a refusal — never a silent redirect to another run.

completed_summaries.description: Map of step name -> summary markdown text.

oneOf.description: Regular (non-parallel, non-delegation) step. Composite driving 7.2: a SUBAGENT step's envelope is SLIM — the engine composes the full task into prompt_file (inject:file content inlined) and the block fields (goal…run_token_text) are ABSENT; spawn with spawn_prompt verbatim. An INLINE (subagent: false) step carries the full blocks instead and has no prompt_file/spawn_prompt.

spec_guidance_text.description: Unified spec guidance (spec-capability policy): consumption and/or authoring bodies with a single shared concept preamble + domain landscape. Empty when neither spec_check nor spec_authoring is set.

run_token_text.description: HTML comment to inject into subagent task: <!--workflow:run_token:UUID-->

gate.description: Composite driving: the resolved quality-gate flags — both false → step_complete directly after the subagent (it validates the verdict itself); either true → step_collect_result first, as before.

oneOf.description: Parallel step (parallel: true). One entry per branch.
Refusal / error envelope — no `type` discriminator. Carries an ORCHESTRATOR DIRECTIVE in `error` and, for engine refusals, an `action` from the step_begin subset (strict-cursor and ownership guards).

step.description: Expected step name (used for staleness detection).

step_collect_result_output.description: Decision for the orchestrator's next move. Several variants exist; the discriminator is the combination of `action`, `passed`, and presence of `error`/`warning`/`stale`.

action.$comment: A fresh-spawn RETRY_STEP normally also carries retry_begin (composite driving): the regenerated prompt file (with a Retry Feedback section) + spawn_prompt, spawned verbatim.
action.description: The three live decisions, plus the ownership refusal (the entry guard returns {error, action, tool} — a worker calling from a foreign engine process). VERIFY_MANUALLY is historical: a foreign verdict is re-validated inline instead of asking for arbitration; kept so old artifacts validate.

summary.description: Brief 2-3 sentence summary of what the step accomplished.

oneOf.description: Step marked complete — plain success (no `action`) or an engine-owned control-flow verdict (`action` set; obey it: LOOP_BACK / ENTER_ROUTE moved the cursor, ENTER_LANES registered the fork's lanes and LANE_WAIT parks a finished lane while siblings run, the AWAITING pair suspends for a decision round-trip).

lanes.description: ENTER_LANES: the {lane id → first step} map.

lanes_exit.description: The join barrier passed: per-lane verdicts; the cursor is already past the fork.

next_begin.description: Composite driving: the admitted next step's complete step_begin payload — present on every successful terminal advance with a known target (plain advance, LOOP_BACK, ENTER_ROUTE); AWAITING_*/error envelopes never carry it. Absent on an advance = degraded compose — call step_begin as before.

lanes_begin.description: Composite driving, ENTER_LANES only: one full step_begin payload per lane, keyed by lane id. A lane absent from the map is driven via step_begin.

oneOf.description: Refusal / error envelope — the step is NOT complete. FIX_AND_RETRY (safety-net validation or delegation handoff; `validation_errors` when validation produced them), STOP_WORKFLOW (decider failure), USER_REJECTED / AWAITING_HUMAN_RESPONSE (inbox human gate), BLOCKED_PARTIAL_FAILURE (unresolved branch failures), BLOCKED_FOREIGN_CALLER (ownership guard).
